updated_interrupts.game_note: M8.4 (owner, 28 Sep 2026): a live full-stack AI cloud with >= min_gpus GPUs rolls once a quarter at chance_pct (mine, from the pack's 'random'); a hit fails failed_share_range of its GPUs (uniform, rounded up). Choices: replace now (replace_cost_usd_per_gpu each, no lost revenue; the default) or run short (no cash now; the failed GPUs earn nothing for the rest of the quarter and the next, a contracted tenant gets an SLA credit of sla_credit_mult x the lost revenue, and the replacement is paid at the end of the next quarter). Counts toward the 3-interrupt cap; with the cap full it resolves silently with the default.
updated_interrupts.magnitude: at cluster scale, model a 'failure wave' roughly every 3-4 hours of game-time-equivalent, each event taking out 0.5-1% of the active cluster (matches Meta Llama 3: 148 GPU-level incidents / 16,384 GPUs ≈ 0.9% of fleet over a 54-day run)
updated_interrupts.cause_split: GPU + HBM3 memory failures ≈50% of incidents; remainder software/network/CPU (CPUs are far more reliable at this scale)
updated_interrupts.cost_model: repair/replace ≈$30,000 per failed GPU (hardware-only) if full replacement is needed; most incidents are short (hours), automated-recovery events (Meta maintained >90% effective training time despite ~7.76 unexpected interruptions/day)
updated_interrupts.source: Tom's Hardware / DataCenterDynamics reporting on Meta's Llama 3 training run failure report (sourced)

sla_penalty_pct_mrc.source: typical colocation SLA: below-99% uptime triggers a 15% monthly-recurring-charge credit, capped at 50% MRC/month (Advanced Hosting colo SLA; DCD SLA-risk guide)
